deep.reconstruction:
This page is printed text from an arithmetic textbook on indeterminate (Diophantine) problems, continuing p.109. Only the right margin is handwritten, and it is cut off; its full version is on the next page.

PRINTED PROBLEM 4 (taken from Hemeling). A farm woman sells x geese at 10 Mgr, y hens at 6 Mgr, z ducks at 4 Mgr and t pigeons at 2 Mgr. She sells 140 animals in all and takes 26 Rthl 24 Mgr. With 1 Rthl = 36 Mgr (my conversion), the takings are 960 Mgr.
- The equations are x+y+z+t = 140 and 10x+6y+4z+2t = 960.
- Halving the second gives 5x+3y+2z+t = 480.
- Subtracting the first leaves 4x+2y+z = 340, so x = 85 - y/2 - z/4.
- The author sets y = 2p and z = 4q, giving x = 85 - p - q, so p+q < 85. Then t = 140-x-y-z = 55 + p - 3q (my general form).
- Case p = q: x = 85-2q, y = 2q, z = 4q, t = 55-4q. Requiring t > 0 gives q ≤ 13, hence 13 solutions in the printed table, q = 1..13.
- Case p = 2q: x = 85-3q, y = z = 4q, t = 55-5q = 5(11-q). So q ≤ 11, but q = 11 gives t = 0, hence 'eigentlich nur 10 Fälle'.
- Hemeling's answer (60, 40, 20, 20) is the case p = 2q, q = 5.

MARGINAL NOTES (Gauss's hand). These are a fragment of a calculation of log 10037 by the 'near-product' trick.
- The factorization is 10037·97·691 + 1 = 672750000 = 225·10^4·299.
- Hence log 10037 = log 10^4 + log 225 + log 299 - log 97 - log 691 + log(1 - 1/a), with a = 672750000.
- The correction term uses 1/672.75 = 4/2691 = 2/9 + 9/13 + 2/23 - 1. A partial-fraction split over 2691 = 9·13·23 lets the term be written as repeating decimals.
- The digit strings '9145 2991…' and '869 565…' are the periodic decimals 107/117 = 2/9 + 9/13 = 0.914529914529… and 2/23 = 0.0869565217391304347826….
- The cut-off lines 'a pq +, a' qr +, …' belong to the cyclic system of equations on the next page.
errors: The printed parametrization y=2p, z=4q is sufficient but not necessary. The true condition from 4x+2y+z=340 is only 2y+z ≡ 0 (mod 4). It allows y odd with z ≡ 2 (mod 4), e.g. (x,y,z,t) = (84,1,2,53), which is a valid solution that the method misses.
Treating only p=q and p=2q is illustrative, not exhaustive; the author admits this.
Whether q=0 or t=0 cases count is handled informally (the '11 oder eigentlich nur 10' remark).
The printed arithmetic in both cases and in the 13-column table is correct.
The marginal identities are all exactly correct: 10037·97·691+1 = 672750000 and 2/9+9/13+2/23-1 = 4/2691 = 1/672.75.
